2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l77.c7/text:
“Too close to call!”

The state of Florida has a margin of victory under half a percent, and with the election hinging on its result, the recounts in the state are going to decide it. Every court option and legal procedure will be investigated by you and your opponent, so be ready for the long haul. Let’s hope this delay in fundamental democracy doesn't result in the unpreparedness of any critical governmental agencies. That would be truly terrible!
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l81.c6/text:
“GOD FUCKING DAMNIT GORE”

Those words rang out from the president's office, despite the door being shut. In the room, were President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.'I BROUGHT THE ECONOMY BACK FROM A TERRIBLE STATE RUN BY INCOMPETENT REPUBLICANS. I WON DURING THE MID-TERMS AND GAVE YOU A FREE TICKET TO THE PRESIDENCY. AND WHAT DO YOU DO? YOU LET THE SON OF THE GUY WHO I BEAT BECOME PRESIDENT! 538 VOTES TO 0!' Those were the words of a less than happy Bill Clinton. Gore responded 'I-I don't know what happened, I-I thought I ran a good campaign b-but...' Clinton interrupted, saying 'You know exactly what happened Gore. For some reason, you did a tank photo op like Dukakis, which is already bad enough. BUT THEN you accidentally fired the tank, I have no clue how, those things are hard to fire, and you hit a group of spectators. Killing 5. Your court date is in a month so you better start prepping a defence team.' 'co-' 'If you’re asking me for a pardon, you can shove it. Then in your speech to the nation about it, you claimed the ghost of William Mckinley had fired the tank by controlling your body. You then spent 50 thousand dollars of taxpayer money on hiring an exorcist to try and remove him. That’s why you lost, Al.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l100.c28/text: You still have many options for your political career as of now. You are still popular in your party and Texas, so there is no doubt you can still influence the next candidate. Perhaps it will be you, or your brother. Maybe the American public will get sick of the Bush family and choose someone else entirely. Whatever the case, let’s hope the Republicans can recover as the Democrats did 8 years ago.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l103.c31/text: Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. The closeness of the election will likely inspire Gore to be a bit more moderate and bipartisan in his decision-making. With the close Senate, it will certainly be needed.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l106.c31/text: Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. 2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l113.c28/text: For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Republicans enraged, especially due to the fact this is the 3rd Democrat in a row winning with less than 50% of the popular vote. Maybe a run in 4 years IS in the books for you...
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l117.c28/text: What will happen next is up to you, although most people have some expectations. Tax cuts will certainly be going into effect, and some bills related to gay marriage or homosexual people in the military will as well. Just keep an eye out for 2004, and don't make the same mistakes as your dad.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l120.c31/text: Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. Your impressive margin allows the Senate and House to stay in Republican hands, with a Republican president for the first time since Dwight Eisenhower!
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l124.c31/text: Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You've managed to flip a few seats in the house and Senate, but it's best you act quickly on your promises or the midterms could take that all away.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l128.c31/text: Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You barely won, however, so let’s hope your bipartisanship and compassionate conservativism resonate with many Americans.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l132.c29/text: For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Democrats are very angry, especially at Ralph Nader for "spoiling" the election.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l141.c28/text: It's up to you what you want to do next. A run in 4 years isn't totally out of the question, but after your decades in politics, you might be burnt out. In any case, let’s hope Bush can continue the economic prosperity and tone down the foreign policy intervention, such as in Somalia. Anything more like that would be a disaster...

Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. At least with the close margin, Bush's bipartisanship will have to be on full display.

2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l166.c28/text: Interestingly enough, you've lost the popular vote despite winning overall, for the first time since 1888. Republicans aren't too happy about losing 3 elections in a row to someone who won less than 50% of the popular vote.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l174.c12/text:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

Congratulations! You received 5% of the popular vote! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. You’ve run a great campaign these last few months, and you should have no problem getting renominated in 4 years.

But for now, sit back and relax, you’ve earned it. Who knows? Maybe next election you’ll even win a state or two.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l178.c12/text:
”Congratulations! You’ve won D.C.!”

What a campaign! You’ve managed to surpass expectations and net yourself some electoral votes! You should have no trouble gaining federal matching funds next election, and you can take solace in the fact that the people of D.C. chose the only capable man this election.

Democrats are sure to be miffed, especially so if they lost, but you couldn’t care less at this moment. Good luck in 2004!
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l182.c9/text:
”Holy Cow! You won a state!”

Everyone thought it impossible, but you’ve pulled it off! You’re the first third-party candidate in over 30 years to win a state, and both you and your supporters are ecstatic. Federal matching funds in 2004 are all but guaranteed, and you’ve established the green party as a force to be reckoned with.

Let’s hope you’re more than just a flash in the pan and can run a similar campaign in 2004. The Green party may even find itself in the White House someday - and it’s all thanks to you.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l186.c12/text:
”The Senate will now vote on H.R. 5411, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001.”

Those were the words of the clerk in the US Senate. They went through each Senator by state, asking for a voice vote from each of them. After all, was said and done, the tally was 81-19 in favour of the motion. the clerk said 'The motion passes. The bill will now be presented to the president for signing.' He stood up and turned around, only to see president Ralph Nader standing 2 inches behind him, which causes the Clerk to stumble back. 'Oh, h-hello there President Nader. I was just going to pres-' He gets interrupted by the loudest yell he had ever heard, when president Nader bellowed at him:

VETOED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

president Nader then had his 74th veto overridden that congress just 5 minutes later.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l190.c12/text:
”Good lord! You’ve won the 2000 election!”

Everyone thought it impossible, that at best you would get 5%, but you’ve proved everybody wrong! This is the biggest political upset in American history, beating out Truman over 50 years ago. An impromptu party has been arranged at the Green Party headquarters in DC, your answering machine is clogged with congratulatory calls from your supporters, and every news station in the country has been clamouring to get to you for an interview

What you've achieved tonight is a stellar victory that will be studied for the rest of American history. From Nader’s Raiders to the White House in 30 years, let’s hope your surprise victory has also netted the Green Party some senate seats, or you’ll have to compromise big in the coming years, considering your stiff opposition from both parties. This definitely wasn’t supposed to happen - Good luck!
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l194.c10/text:
"It is Over"

The results are coming in, and the phone is ringing. You reach slowly into your drawer and pull out something you never thought you would use. The TV announcer drawls, "The biggest loser of tonight is Ralph Nader! Nader appears to have only received
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l194.c305/text:
votes nationwide." You pull the gun to your head, and slowly press on the trigger... and then there was nothing.

A noise suddenly grabs your attention, but your vision is still fuzzy.

"Ralph, cmon!"

The voice seems strained. Your vision suddenly clears. You are in a white room. As your eyes trail sluggishly around the room, you notice something strange. There are a series of glass pods lining the sides of the room. In each pod, there is a person inside each, with every person having some form of cap on their head.

"Get out of the simulator, Ralph! We have some shopping to do," and then finally, you remembered.
2000_Bush_Ridge/ending/s0.l198.c12/text:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3312@0/desc: We need to expand benefits for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. We can use the surplus as well as defense cuts to balance these increases.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3310@1/desc: We should enact tax cuts to return this money to the American people. My plan will reduce the burden for all Americans who currently pay income tax.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3311@2/desc: We should try to keep things as they are. The economy has been unusually good the past few years, and we already have a large federal debt to pay down.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3313@3/desc: I would prefer to see us allocate this money to new and existing government programs so that all Americans can share in our prosperity.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3314@4/desc: I believe that we need to return control of education to the states and to the people. I would end the Department of Education as President.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3315@5/desc: Many schools are squandering the resources of the federal government. I support providing school vouchers directly to parents, so that they can choose where their child goes.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3316@6/desc: We need more spending for America's struggling schools, and national standards and testing to identify and fix poor performers. Every child deserves a strong, functional school to attend.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3317@7/desc: We need to increase pay for teachers and increase funding for the Department of Education. I don't support nationwide standards or testing -- they will distort the learning process and lead to education by rote.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3318@8/desc: The Social Security system is a financial time bomb. We need to get rid of it, or at the very least cut its benefits significantly.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3319@9/desc: The average worker would do much better if their money was invested in the stock market. I support a plan to allow workers to contribute at least some of their Social Security contribution to an individual investment account.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3320@10/des: I would establish an iron-clad lockbox for the Social Security fund. When we allow the federal government to borrow our Social Security money, we put every senior in this country at risk.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3321@11/des: We need to increase benefits for Social Security. Many people can barely survive on the monthly payment, while we spend billions on the military and run a huge budget surplus.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3322@12/des: The Cold War is over. We should cut defense spending and stop operating so many bases overseas. I would pull troops out of places like Germany and Okinawa, where we are no longer defending anything.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3323@13/des: America should remain tough, but humble. I am concerned about some of our recent interventions in places like Somalia and Serbia.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3324@14/des: We need to remain an engaged, committed defender of human rights in the world. We should do everything possible to secure the friendship of nations like Russia and China, and to prevent atrocities and genocide in the developing world.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3325@15/des: I would focus on removing dictators like Saddam Hussein and Kim Jong Il from power. They threaten the stability of the world and perpetrate evil upon their people.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3326@16/des: Bill Clinton was an embarrassment to the United States, and his impeachment was well-deserved. I believe that he should have been removed from office.
2000_Bush_Ridge/answers_json/3327@17/des: I don't think we need to belabor the point. I pledge to the American people that I will restore honor and dignity to the White House when I am President.
